name: Adoniram Judson
title: Adoniram Judson: persevering so others could read the Bible
description: Learning Burmese, translating the Bible, and the losses of the Judson family let us look at mission with gratitude and humanity.

sections.heading: Learning before being able to communicate
paragraphs: Adoniram Judson and Ann Hasseltine married and sailed from the United States to Asia in 1812. A change in their convictions about baptism led them to leave their sending organization and seek new sources of support. Their missionary path included doctrinal decisions with practical consequences.

Learning the Burmese language and culture was central to his work. Judson translated the Bible into Burmese and prepared language tools. That effort made it possible to read the Scriptures without depending on knowing the missionary’s language.

sections.heading: Perseverance had a human cost
paragraphs: During the war between Burma and Britain, Judson was imprisoned in 1824 on suspicion of spying. Ann worked to get food and help for him. The IMB’s institutional biography highlights that service, which lets us see an essential partner in the midst of an extreme situation.

Ann’s death in 1826, and their daughter’s shortly afterward, plunged him into deep grief. He later continued his translation work and his support of other workers. He died in 1850. His story holds both the value of the work accomplished and the weight of the losses.

reflection: In 2 Corinthians 4:7–9, Paul describes the frailty of those who carry the message of Christ. Devotion to the gospel goes hand in hand with weariness, danger, and the need to receive help. Recognizing this helps us better support those who serve and keeps us from turning their suffering into a requirement for proving faithfulness.

Bible translation also teaches a patient kind of love: studying so that someone else can understand. In a local church, that attitude shows itself in explaining a difficult word, preparing an accessible lesson, or listening to how a person is understanding the text. Clarity takes work and humility.
review_note: Ann’s role is acknowledged, and grief is not treated as a lack of faith. Conversion figures and stories about the preservation of the manuscript, which would need further checking, are left out.
source_labels: Nathan Finn, International Mission Board. “Missionaries You Should Know: Adoniram Judson” (March 27, 2018).
source_kinds: Institutional biography from a Baptist perspective
